title: Weak equivalences survive simplicial interval cell attachments
statement: Use the category $\mathrm{sCat}$ and the generating families $I,J$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For $F:A\to B$, call $F$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence if each $A(a,a')\to B(Fa,Fa')$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $\pi_0F$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories. The class $W$ of Dwyer--Kan equivalences is closed under retracts and satisfies two-out-of-three. Every relative $J\text{-cell}$ map belongs to $W$: this includes transfinite composites, with the category at each limit ordinal the colimit of all earlier stages, of arbitrary pushouts of coproducts of the horn and countable interval maps specified there. No local Kan condition on the categories at the stages of the cell construction is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1; Lemma 3.4 and the cell-construction argument in the proof of Proposition 3.3, pp. 10–12 of the article. No Stacks tag states the enriched interval pushout lemma.

proof.text: First record how an isomorphism in $\pi_0C$ changes the objects of a mapping set. Represent it and its inverse by vertices $e:a\to b$ and $v:b\to a$. The vertices $ve,ev$ are connected to the relevant identity vertices by finite zigzags of edges in the mapping sets. To identify this edge relation with path components of realization, partition vertices by finite edge zigzags. All vertices of any simplex are joined by its edges, so the simplicial set is the disjoint union of the simplicial subsets belonging to these classes. Realization preserves that disjoint union by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]; each resulting summand is path connected because every point in a realized simplex can be joined inside that simplex to a vertex, and the vertices are joined by the edge zigzags. Thus these summands are precisely the path components. Composition with each edge defines a map $\Delta^1\times C(z,a)\to C(z,a)$, or the corresponding map for precomposition. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], realization naturally preserves finite products in the category $\mathcal K$ of k-spaces, and the realized pair $(|\Delta^1|,|\partial\Delta^1|)$ is an interval with its two endpoints. Thus realization of the displayed simplicial map gives a homotopy, with parameter $[0,1]$, of the corresponding composition maps in $\mathcal K$. Thus the realized compositions with $e$ and $v$ are mutually inverse up to homotopy (concatenate the finitely many homotopies, reversing their direction when necessary). In particular composition with $e$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on all affected mapping sets. The argument applies to arbitrary simplicial mapping sets.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, expansion of the object-transport used in two-out-of-three; agent supplies the edge-zigzag argument

proof.text: We prove two-out-of-three for $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$. If $f,g$ are DK-equivalences, their composite is locally a weak equivalence by the simplicial-set two-out-of-three property [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and its component functor is an equivalence by composing fully faithful essentially surjective functors. If $g,gf$ are DK-equivalences, local two-out-of-three gives the local property for $f$; for any $b\in B$, essential surjectivity of $gf$ gives an isomorphism $gf(a)\cong g(b)$, and full faithfulness of $\pi_0g$ lifts it and its inverse to an isomorphism $f(a)\cong b$. If $f,gf$ are DK-equivalences, $g$ is essentially surjective because $gf$ is; local two-out-of-three first proves its local property on pairs $f(a),f(a')$. For arbitrary $b,b'$, choose isomorphisms $f(a)\cong b$ and $f(a')\cong b'$ in $\pi_0B$. Choose vertices $e:f(a)\to b$, $e':f(a')\to b'$ and a vertex $v:b\to f(a)$ representing the inverse of $e$. The comparison map $B(f(a),f(a'))\to B(b,b')$ sends $k$ to $e'kv$. On the $C$-mapping sets use $g(e')(-)g(v)$. These maps commute strictly with $g$ by preservation of composition; both comparison maps are weak equivalences by step 1. The composite from $B(f(a),f(a'))$ to $C(gb,gb')$ is therefore a weak equivalence, and two-out-of-three with the first comparison map proves the local property for $g$ at $(b,b')$. A locally weak equivalence is fully faithful after $\pi_0$, which completes each case. For a retract $f:A\to B$ of a DK-equivalence $h:A'\to B'$ in the arrow category, each mapping-set map of $f$ is a retract of that of $h$ at the section images of its objects, hence a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For $b\in B$, apply essential surjectivity of $h$ to the section image of $b$ and apply the retraction functor to its witnessing isomorphism. This gives $f(a)\cong b$ and proves retract closure.

source.place: Proposition 3.1; complete verification of retract closure and all three two-out-of-three cases

proof.text: Consider a horn cell attached to a simplicial category $C$ with object set $O$. Its attaching functor sends the two objects to some $a,b\in O$, possibly equal. Let $F_{a,b}(K)$ denote the free $O$-object simplicial category on a simplicial set of arrows $K$ from $a$ to $b$: in each degree its morphisms are composable words in these generators, including empty identity words; faces and degeneracies act on each letter. Maps $F_{a,b}(K)\to T$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ are exactly simplicial maps $K\to T(a,b)$. The variable-object horn pushout is the fixed-object pushout of $F_{a,b}(\Lambda_i^n)\to F_{a,b}(\Delta^n)$. To check this even against a target $T$ with arbitrary object set, fix a functor $C\to T$. An extension over either proposed pushout is exactly a simplicial map $\Delta^n\to T(Fa,Fb)$ restricting to the prescribed horn map. The object choices are already fixed by $C\to T$ because the horn generator changes no objects. For the fixed-object calculation use the $O$-labelled category $T_F$ with $T_F(s,t)=T(Fs,Ft)$ and identities and compositions from $T$, even when different labels have the same image. The free-arrow bijection applied to $T_F$ gives the same extensions on the fixed-object side, and their uniqueness proves the variable-object pushout universal property. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] horns have the left lifting property against all Kan fibrations; the displayed bijection of maps translates a lifting square against an objectwise fibration in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ into precisely such a horn square. Hence this free horn map, and its pushout $C\to D$, have the left lifting property against every fibration in the fixed-object model of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. The model axioms make $C\to D$ a trivial cofibration there. It is locally a weak equivalence, fixes all objects, and is consequently a DK-equivalence. When $a=b$ the free words are loops, and the bijection of maps just proved still sends a generator to an arbitrary simplex of $T(a,a)$; its horn-lifting conclusion therefore includes coincident attaching objects.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, horn case; explicit free-arrow/lifting argument also treating coincident attaching objects

proof.text: For an interval cell write $D=C\amalg_{\{x\}}H$, renaming the attaching object of $C$ as $x$, and write $y$ for the other, new object of $H$. Put $O=\operatorname{Ob}C$ and $X=O\amalg\{y\}$. A set used as an enriched category here is discrete (identity mapping sets $\Delta^0$, all other mapping sets empty). Put $C'=C\amalg\{y\}$ and $H'=(O\setminus\{x\})\amalg H$. Then $D=H'\amalg_X C'$ by the pushout universal property, and $X\to H'$ is a cofibration in $\mathrm{sCat}_X$: a lifting problem against an objectwise trivial fibration restricts to the given cofibration of $H$ on $\{x,y\}$; at the other objects only identities need lifting. Choose a cofibrant replacement $q:C_0\to C$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ by factoring the map from the discrete category $O$ (the initial object of $\mathrm{sCat}_O$) to $C$ as a cofibration $O\to C_0$ followed by an objectwise trivial Kan fibration $q$, using the model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]; thus $q$ is in particular an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. Set $C''=C_0\amalg\{y\}$. To lift $X\to C''$ against an objectwise trivial fibration $T\to S$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_X$, restrict its square to $O$ and lift $O\to C_0$ using cofibrancy of $C_0$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. Extend this lift at $y$ by its required identity map $\Delta^0\to T(y,y)$; every mapping set from $y$ to $O$ or from $O$ to $y$ in $C''$ is empty, so its unique map imposes no further condition. This is an enriched lift, proving $X\to C''$ is a cofibration. The map $q'=q\amalg1:C''\to C'$ is an objectwise trivial fibration: its restriction to $O$ is $q$, its new off-diagonal maps are $\varnothing\to\varnothing$, and its new endomorphism map is $\Delta^0\to\Delta^0$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, interval case, printed pp. 10-11; choose the replacement to leave the new isolated object unchanged

proof.text: Let $E$ be the disjoint union of the discrete category on $O\setminus\{x\}$ with the ordinary groupoid on $x,y$ having exactly one morphism for each ordered pair, regarded as a constant simplicial category. The canonical functor $h:H'\to E$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence: each of the four mapping sets of $H$ is weakly contractible; all remaining mapping-set maps are identities. Define $D''=H'\amalg_X C''$ and $P''=E\amalg_X C''$. The map $D''\to D$ is the pushout of $q'$ along the cofibration $C''\to D''$ obtained from $X\to H'$. The map $D''\to P''$ is the pushout of $h$ along the cofibration $H'\to D''$ obtained from $X\to C''$. The two asserted cofibrations can be checked directly from the lifting definition: a square from a pushout inclusion against a trivial fibration restricts to a square from the original cofibration; its lift and the given map from the other leg agree on $X$, so glue to the required lift. Both maps are objectwise weak equivalences by [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-left-proper]. These are two applications of left properness in $\mathrm{sCat}_X$, with all stated cofibration hypotheses checked; neither is an appeal to an as-yet-unconstructed variable-object model structure.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, interval case, comparisons of the three fixed-object spans, printed p. 11

proof.text: Compute $P''$ explicitly. Let $r:X\to O$ be the identity on $O$ and send $y$ to $x$. The category with mapping sets $P''(u,v)=C_0(r(u),r(v))$ and composition inherited from $C_0$ is the required pushout. Indeed a compatible pair of enriched functors from $C''$ and $E$ to any simplicial category $T$ consists of a functor from $C_0$, an object for $y$, and a strict isomorphism $u:T(x)\to T(y)$. Its unique extension sends a morphism in $C_0(r(s),r(t))$ to $u_t\,F(-)\,u_s^{-1}$, where $u_s=1$ for $s\in O$ and $u_y=u$. These formulas preserve composition because $u_s^{-1}u_s=1$, and prove the universal property. In particular the composite $C_0\to D''\to P''$ induces the identity of $C_0(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in O$. Since $D''\to P''$ is locally a weak equivalence, local two-out-of-three makes $C_0(a,b)\to D''(a,b)$ a weak equivalence. In the square with horizontal maps $C_0(a,b)\to D''(a,b)$ and $C(a,b)\to D(a,b)$ the vertical maps are weak equivalences by $q$ and step 5. Thus $C(a,b)\to D(a,b)$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Finally $D$ has exactly the objects $O\amalg\{y\}$, and the vertices of $H(x,y)$ and $H(y,x)$ give inverse arrows in $\pi_0D$: their two composites and the identities have the same components since $\pi_0H$ has one arrow per ordered pair. Hence $C\to D$ is essentially surjective and is a DK-equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, printed p. 11: expanded duplicate-object pushout calculation and deduction of the actual local maps

proof.text: A continuous ordinal sequence $C_\alpha$ of these single-cell attachments has injective object maps: a horn cell keeps the object set and an interval cell adds precisely one new object. At a nonzero limit ordinal $\lambda$, the object set of $C_\lambda$ is their union. For objects $a,b$ occurring by a stage $\beta<\lambda$, its mapping set is $C_\lambda(a,b)=\varinjlim_{\beta\leq\alpha<\lambda} C_\alpha(a,b)$. To verify this formula without a Kan assumption, form the degreewise colimit of the mapping sets on the union of objects: two representatives are equal just when their images agree at a later stage. Two composable representatives occur together at some stage, so their composite is defined there and is independent of the chosen stage. Associativity, units and simplicial operators hold because each involves only finitely many representatives and equations, all verifiable at a common later stage. The resulting enriched category has exactly the colimit universal property. No assertion that arbitrary enriched pushouts are pointwise is being used.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.3, directed-colimit sentence; explicit filtered enriched-colimit construction

proof.text: Prove by transfinite induction that every $C_0\to C_\alpha$ is a DK-equivalence. The identity is the base case; the successor case is steps 3 and 6 followed by step 2. At a nonzero limit $\lambda$, fix $a,b\in C_0$. The tail of ordinals below $\lambda$ is a nonempty filtered category, and the compatible maps from the constant simplicial set $C_0(a,b)$ to $C_\alpha(a,b)$ are weak equivalences by induction. The colimit of this constant source diagram is $C_0(a,b)$: all transition maps are identities, and any two stages have a common later stage, so the colimit identifies precisely the copies of the same simplex. Apply [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] and the explicit colimit of step 7 to obtain the local weak equivalence into $C_\lambda$. Every object $z\in C_\lambda$ occurs at an earlier stage, where the inductive essential-surjectivity assertion supplies an isomorphism between $z$ and the image of an object of $C_0$. Its vertices and inverse relations remain such in the colimit, so essential surjectivity also holds. If $C_0$ is empty there are no intervals to attach (their singleton domain has no map to it), and no horn domain admits an object map either; the sequence stays empty. Thus this edge case also satisfies the induction.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.3, transfinite cell-construction argument; limit step supplied by Kerodon Tag 00XE

proof.text: For the arbitrary coproducts in a relative $J$-cell presentation, well-order the set of cells attached at each successor stage and attach them singly in that order, composing each original attaching map with the current structure map. At every intermediate limit take the colimit. A functor from the result to any $T$ is exactly a functor from the starting stage together with an extension over each original cell agreeing on its domain: this proves that the refined result is the original simultaneous pushout. The same universal-property argument identifies the colimits after concatenating these refinements over the original ordinal presentation. Apply step 8 to this single-cell refinement. The empty family and the zero-length construction give identities. We have proved every asserted relative $J$-cell map is in $W$, with no fibrancy restriction, as well as retract closure and two-out-of-three from step 2.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.3; expansion from iterated single cells to arbitrary coproduct cells and continuous transfinite presentations
